clauses.current_legal_basis: The delegation in section 1, as amended by EO 11382 and EO 13286, is printed as a current note under 10 U.S.C. 10149 in the held U.S. Code release point 119-121; no held instrument revokes or supersedes it.

later_events.mechanism: amendment by striking the Secretary of the Treasury and inserting the Secretary of Transportation; the clause continues as amended

amendment by striking the Secretary of Transportation in section 1 and inserting the Secretary of Homeland Security (EO 13286 section 67; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92); the clause continues as amended

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 delegates the section 271 authority (title 10) to the Secretary of Defense and, for the Coast Guard, to another Secretary; the order has no end of its own and two later orders only substituted that other Secretary's title (before-and-after: the Treasury, then Transportation, then Homeland Security). The delegation is still printed as a note in the current U.S. Code, so the command continues, amended.

Section 2 reads 'Sec. 2. Executive Order No. 10651 of January 6,1956, is revoked.' It is a self-executing revocation with no later date or condition, so it was performed when the order took effect on its signing date, 1964-12-29 (the order states no other effective date); the revocation of EO 10651 then stands as accomplished, and nothing in the held sources shows a later end or revival.

research_rationale:
EO 11190 (signed 1964-12-29; 29 FR 19183, filed 1964-12-30, printed 1964-12-31) has two operative sections: section 1 delegates to the Secretary of Defense (and, for the Coast Guard, to a second Secretary) the President's authority under section 271 of title 10, U.S. Code, to prescribe regulations for screening the Ready Reserve; section 2 revokes EO 10651 of January 6, 1956. I read the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11190.txt in full; number, title, signer and FR page match the register row (the OCR of the signing date line is garbled; the register and the FR citation give 1964-12-29). Later instruments naming the order: EO 11382 (signed 1967-11-28, 32 FR 16247) strikes out the Secretary of the Treasury and inserts the Secretary of Transportation in this order (it lists EO 11190 among the orders so amended), and EO 13286 section 67 (signed 2003-02-28, 68 FR 10619; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) strikes the Secretary of Transportation in section 1 and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security. Both are strike-and-insert amendments, recorded as later events under the 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling; the clause continues, amended. The held U.S. Code text (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order as a note under 10 U.S.C. 10149, headed 'Ex. Ord. No. 11190. Screening of Ready Reserve', with the status line 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 11382, Nov. 28, 1967, 32 F.R. 16247; Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 67, Feb. 28, 2003, 68 F.R. 10630', and with section 1 naming the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard. The eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) found no hit naming this order. No revocation of EO 11190 appears in the held Federal Register disposition notes (which list only the two amendments) or in the held texts that cite the order's number (a 1999 Federal Register notice cites it for the screening program). The delegation therefore had not ended by 2026-10-14. Section 2 is a self-executing revocation of EO 10651, performed when the order took effect.

savings.reason: The order has no savings or transition clause. The only surviving effect apart from the continuing delegation in section 1 is that EO 10651 stays revoked, which is the performed section 2 and needs no separate source.
